options: Silphium was so highly valued by Greek and Roman writers that it was used to treat everything from coughs to indigestion.
Because silphium grew only in a narrow region near Cyrene and resisted cultivation elsewhere, merchants had to rely entirely on wild plants harvested from that limited habitat.
Cyrene's economy was so dependent on silphium that the plant's image was placed on the city's coins.
Pliny the Elder noted that silphium had become extremely rare by the first century CE, likely due to overharvesting and habitat loss.
before.explanation: 학생의 목표는 '왜 실피움 무역을 수요 증가에 맞춰 확장할 수 없었는지' 설명하는 것이다. 이는 재배 불가능성(공급 제약의 원인)과 관련된 정보를 종합해야 한다. B는 메모 1(좁은 서식지)과 메모 3(재배 불가로 야생 채집에만 의존)을 결합하여 공급 확장이 불가능했던 구조적 이유를 정확히 제시한다. A는 실피움의 인기와 용도만 설명할 뿐 공급 확장 불가 이유와 무관하다(목표 무시). C는 경제 의존도와 화폐 도안이라는 하나의 메모만 사용했을 뿐 공급 제약과는 무관하다(단일 메모 오용). D는 플리니우스의 기록과 멸종 원인을 결합했지만, 이는 실피움이 '이미 희귀해진 결과'를 설명할 뿐 애초에 왜 공급을 늘릴 수 없었는지에 대한 답은 아니다(잘못된 메모 결합).

options: Ancient Greek and Roman writers praised silphium as a seasoning and as a treatment for a wide range of ailments, from coughs to indigestion.
Because silphium grew only in a narrow region near Cyrene and resisted cultivation elsewhere, merchants had to rely entirely on wild plants harvested from that limited habitat.
Because Cyrene's economy depended heavily on the silphium trade, the plant's image appeared on the city's coins, showing how valuable the plant was.
All commercial supplies of silphium came from wild plants harvested in the narrow region near Cyrene, so demand for the plant grew rapidly among Greek and Roman consumers.
